solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Small change to sponsor senior primate (10)

blocks.note: silver is loose coins of low value
to back is to support financially

annotation.surface: Someone proposes funding a gorilla with a bit of loose change.
annotation.walkthrough: A silverback is the mature male who leads a gorilla troop, hence "senior primate".
annotation.definitionFit: A silverback is an older male gorilla, named for the grey hair on his back.

blocks.note: to sack a city is to plunder and wreck it
the plural noun: large coarse bags for carrying goods

annotation.surface: Something ruins the luggage.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bags" reads as a verb in the surface, but here it is the plural noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Sacking a town means looting and destroying it.

entries.clue: Singletons in one suit lacking support of others? (6,6)

annotation.definition: Singletons in one suit lacking support of others?

blocks.note: the surface pushes the bridge sense, a lone card in a suit; the setter means single people

blocks.clueFragment: in one suit lacking support of others?
blocks.note: one suit alone and unsupported: the suit of love, with nobody beside it

annotation.surface: A bridge player holds a singleton in one suit, unsupported by other cards of that suit.
annotation.walkthrough: The card-table reading of singletons, suit and support is a disguise: singletons are single people, the lonely hearts of dating columns.
annotation.definitionFit: Lonely hearts are single people looking for a partner, as in newspaper lonely hearts ads.

entries.clue: Love god in bedrooms on a regular basis (4)

indicatorNotes.on a regular basis: taking letters at regular intervals, every second one

annotation.surface: The god of love regularly pays a visit to bedrooms.
annotation.walkthrough: Eros is the Greek god of love, and he fits the bedroom scene nicely.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name given by description: the Greek deity of desire, whose Roman counterpart is Cupid.

indicatorNotes.turned: the letters are turned about into a new order

annotation.surface: Embarrassed murmurs as someone turns the tables in an argument.
annotation.walkthrough: "Sheepish" suggests embarrassment, but here it means literally from sheep.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal reading of "sheepish": the noises a sheep makes, rather than the embarrassed kind.

indicatorNotes.about: the scoundrel goes around the other word

blocks.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
to rouse is to stir into action

annotation.surface: A notorious villain is about to cause trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: "Celebrated" poses as the adjective famous, but it is the past tense of celebrate. "About to" looks like a phrase; "about" is the container and "to" belongs to the stir.
annotation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink and celebrate noisily.

indicatorNotes.misrepresented: the letters are presented wrongly, in a new order

annotation.surface: Clumsy wooers got someone's convictions all wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has the suitors as the ones doing the misrepresenting; really their letters are what get jumbled.
annotation.definitionFit: A superstition is an irrational belief, such as that black cats bring bad luck.

blocks.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite

annotation.surface: A child cuddled their favourite teddy bear.
annotation.walkthrough: Cuddled is a verb here, not an adjective describing the bear.
annotation.definitionFit: To pet someone is to stroke or cuddle them affectionately.

indicatorNotes.following: the individual comes after the swindle

annotation.surface: Someone offers comfort to a person who has just been swindled.
annotation.walkthrough: "Comfort" is a verb here, the same part of speech as console.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs for easing another person's grief or disappointment.

entries.clue: Introduction to reading not in English course (5)

indicatorNotes.Introduction to: the introduction of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: out is the opposite of in

annotation.surface: A reading primer that isn't part of the English syllabus.
annotation.walkthrough: "English course" looks like a single school subject; course is the definition alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A route is a course or way taken from one place to another.

indicatorNotes.initially: what a word does initially, at its very start, is its first letter

annotation.surface: Secretaries begin typing up some documents.
annotation.walkthrough: "Type" reads as keyboard work beside secretaries, but it means a kind, ILK.
annotation.definitionFit: Silk is a fine fabric made from silkworm thread.

indicatorNotes.after: the ordeal comes after the beer
indicatorNotes.unfinished: the beer loses its last letter

blocks.note: STOUT, a dark beer, without its final letter
a test is a trial or ordeal

annotation.surface: The hardest trial comes after someone leaves their pint half drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: Stoutest here means most sturdy and resolute, not fattest.
annotation.definitionFit: Stout can mean strong and sturdy, so the stoutest is the toughest.

indicatorNotes.to change: the letters must change their order

annotation.surface: An outrageous scam prompted reform.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a news story about a scandal leading to change; the change is to the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Shocking and dreadful both mean very bad.

annotation.surface: An American travels with a woman acting as her guide.
annotation.walkthrough: "Guide" can be noun or verb, and usher is both.
annotation.definitionFit: An usher guides people to their seats.

entries.clue: Period of activity when I’m awake? (6)

annotation.definition: Period of activity when I’m awake?

blocks.note: the computing sense: the time a system is running
the playful human sense: the hours when a person is up and about

annotation.surface: Someone describes the part of the day when they are awake and busy.
annotation.walkthrough: Uptime is the computing term for when a machine is running; the question mark invites reading it as the time a person is up.
annotation.definitionFit: Uptime is the period during which a computer or system is working.

indicatorNotes.leaderless: the word loses its leader, its first letter

annotation.surface: Someone decides that being without a boss is a relief.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a leaderless group; it is the word CEASED that loses its head.
annotation.definitionFit: Eased and relieved both mean made less painful.

entries.clue: Pave grass over with waterproof coat (6)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, over means turned upside down

blocks.note: to grass is to inform, to rat

annotation.surface: Instructions to pave over the lawn and lay a waterproof covering.
annotation.walkthrough: "Grass" looks like lawn beside "pave", but it is the slang verb to inform on someone. A mac is a mackintosh raincoat.
annotation.definitionFit: A brand-name material used as a verb: to surface a road or drive with tar and stone.

blocks.note: taken literally: pull something off by force

annotation.definitionNote: "Rip off" is the phrase TEAR AWAY, written as one word in the answer.
annotation.surface: A scoundrel cheats someone.
annotation.walkthrough: "Rip off" suggests a swindle, but here it means literally to tear away. A tearaway is a wild, reckless young person.
annotation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a reckless, unruly person, a rascal.

annotation.surface: A robust business.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one adjective and noun; they are two separate definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses of one word: an adjective for solid and unyielding, and a noun for a business.

blocks.note: the Magi, the wise men of the Nativity
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

annotation.surface: Some enigmatic sages have been arrested.
annotation.walkthrough: Magic works as an adjective, as in a magic moment, matching "Mysterious".
annotation.definitionFit: Magic can describe something inexplicable or mysterious in its power.

indicatorNotes.announced: announcing is saying out loud, so we want a sound

blocks.note: a fare is the price of a journey

annotation.surface: The price of a ticket has been announced as reasonable.
annotation.walkthrough: FARE and FAIR are pronounced the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: just and moderate, as in a price nobody can grumble at.

indicatorNotes.returning: going back, so the word is written backwards

annotation.surface: A doctor comes back with a clean bill of health.
annotation.walkthrough: "Healthy figure" suggests a good physique; figure is the definition, in the sense of a pattern or design.
annotation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring figure or design in art or pattern.

indicatorNotes.in play: the letters are played about with

annotation.surface: A team's aim is to gain ground during the game.
annotation.walkthrough: "In play" sounds like a sporting phrase, but it tells you to play with the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of significance or intent, as in the point of life.

indicatorNotes.upset: the letters are upset, knocked out of order

annotation.surface: A vicar is offended by the tone of comments on the internet.
annotation.walkthrough: Both CLERIC and TONE go into the mix; "with" just joins them.
annotation.definitionFit: Something online is carried out electronically, over a computer network.
